title: Glutaric acidaemia type 1
summary: Glutaric acidaemia type 1 means the body cannot break down some building blocks of protein. Harmful substances can build up and damage part of the brain, especially during illness in early childhood.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the GCDH gene from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A child with two changed copies has glutaric acidaemia type 1. Found early, a special diet and an emergency plan for times of illness from a specialist team can prevent much of the harm.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has glutaric acidaemia type 1. Could I be a carrier?
Can glutaric acidaemia type 1 skip a generation?
What does a test for the GCDH gene involve?
card_summary: Some protein building blocks aren't broken down, which can affect the brain. Carriers are healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. A special diet and illness plan from early on can prevent much of the harm.
care: Specialist metabolic and neurology clinics, dietitians, genetic counselling and family support groups.
